cards.name: phase_polynomial_rotation_merge
cards.identity: Partition the op list into maximal contiguous Hadamard-free (and cz-free) segments over the gate set {cx, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz}; an `h` on qubit q ends the segment for q's parity cone (implementation: end the whole segment at any h, then optionally extend per-qubit). Inside a segment, carry for each wire q an affine Z-parity label (p[q] in F2^n over the segment's input basis labels, plus a bit c[q]): initialise p[q]={q}, c[q]=0; `cx a,b` does p[b] ^= p[a], c[b] ^= c[a]; `x a` does c[a] ^= 1; every diagonal rotation g on q (rz(theta), t = rz(pi/4), tdg = rz(-pi/4), s, sdg, z) contributes a term with angle s(q)*theta to the key p[q], where s(q) = +1 if c[q]=0 and -1 if c[q]=1. Two rotation ops i<j in the same segment whose keys p[q_i] and p[q_j] are the EQUAL F2 vector are a match: delete op j and replace op i by rz(theta_eff) with theta_eff = (s_i*theta_i + s_j*theta_j) reduced mod 2pi into (-pi, pi]; if theta_eff == 0 mod 2pi drop the op entirely, if theta_eff is a multiple of pi/4 emit the corresponding Clifford/T gate (with_ops already does this demotion), and if c[q_i]=1 negate back so the stored angle is s_i*theta_eff. Matches are enumerated greedily by descending |theta| so the largest gridsynth costs are retired first.
cards.correctness: Rz, Z, S, T are diagonal in the computational basis and CX/X are basis permutations, so any Hadamard-free segment acts on |x> as a permutation x -> Ax+b (A a CNOT matrix over F2) times a phase exp(i/2 * sum_k s_k theta_k * <p_k, x>-ish) — formally, conjugating Z_q backwards through the CX/X prefix gives the Pauli (-1)^{c[q]} Z^{p[q]}, because CX_{a,b}^dag Z_b CX_{a,b} = Z_a Z_b (parity XOR) and X_q^dag Z_q X_q = -Z_q, while CX and X map Z-type Paulis to Z-type Paulis. Hence rotation op i equals, after commuting it to the segment start, exp(-i s_i theta_i Z^{p[q_i]}/2). If p[q_i] = p[q_j] the two commuted factors are rotations about the SAME Hermitian operator Z^{p}, they commute with everything in between in that representation, and exp(-i a Z^p/2) exp(-i b Z^p/2) = exp(-i (a+b) Z^p/2) since (Z^p)^2 = I. Pushing the merged rotation back to position i through the same Clifford prefix is exact (the prefix is unitary and the conjugation is an identity, not an approximation). Angles add exactly in exact arithmetic; the mod-2pi reduction is exact up to global phase (Rz(2pi) = -I), which invariant 6 permits. Replacement window is Clifford+Rz with equal total angle content, so the frozen judge's phase-aligned distance is 0 (and the exact D[omega] check applies whenever both sides land at pi/4 multiples).
cards.trigger: Fires wherever a Hadamard-free run contains two diagonal rotations whose accumulated affine parity labels coincide. Concretely on qpe_8: scan the 1034-op list, cut at each of the 258 h gates, and inside each of the resulting cx/rz/t/tdg/s/sdg/z runs (the circuit has 268 cx and 257 rz, and the trigram census shows 43x 'cx tdg cx', 29x 'cx t cx', 29x 'tdg cx cx' — i.e. rotations sandwiched inside CX ladders, exactly the configuration where parity labels recur) report every same-key rotation pair. No match is reported across an h, so no Hadamard commutation reasoning is needed.
cards.expected_effect: Each surviving rz costs gridsynth ~57 T at eps_rz = 3.89e-6 (257 rotations x ~57 = 14761, the current count), so every merged pair removes ~57 T and every exact cancellation removes ~114 T. Two signals say the yield is large: (1) the angle histogram contains the exact inverse pair theta=10.566379 and theta=1.999991 with 15 occurrences each, and 10.566379 + 1.999991 = 12.566371 = 4pi to 1e-6, so wherever such a pair shares a parity label the merged angle is 0 and BOTH rotations vanish; likewise 10.566379 mod 2pi = 4.283193 is the exact inverse of 1.999991 mod 2pi. (2) pyzx full_reduce (11485) and BQSKit-DPF (8020) beat TKET's 14761 by 22% and 46% respectively, and the mechanism they both have and TKET's FullPeepholeOptimise lacks is global phase-polynomial rotation merging — this rule is the cheap, locally-verifiable core of it. Estimate 35-60 rotations retired (merges plus the 4pi cancellations), i.e. ~2000-3400 T saved: 14761 -> roughly 11400-12700, in pyzx's range while staying 'exact' contract and spending none of the 5e-4 approximation budget. Also drops zero CNOTs (ties broken on T first, so neutral), and qubit count unchanged at 8.
cards.source: Y. Nam, N. J. Ross, Y. Su, A. M. Childs, D. Maslov, 'Automated optimization of large quantum circuits with continuous parameters', npj Quantum Information 4:23 (2018) — the 'rotation merging in Hadamard-free sub-circuits' pass (their Sec. 4.3 / Rule R-5), with the phase-polynomial parity bookkeeping of Amy, Maslov, Mosca, 'Polynomial-time T-depth optimization of Clifford+T circuits via matroid partitioning' (IEEE TCAD 33(10), 2014) and the affine-parity (X-conjugation sign) extension of Amy & Mosca, 'T-count optimization and Reed-Muller codes' (IEEE Trans. Inf. Theory 65(8), 2019).

cards.name: window_angle_refit_to_clifford_grid
cards.identity: Over-parameterized-window numerical refit. (1) Cut the op list into maximal contiguous windows W with |support(W)| <= 3 qubits and <= 40 ops, containing k >= 3 rotation ops whose angle is NOT a multiple of pi/4 (a window ends at the first op touching a 4th qubit). (2) Freeze W's own Clifford skeleton (its h/s/sdg/x/z/cx/cz ops and their order and wiring) and treat its k non-pi/4 angles as free parameters theta in R^k; the window unitary is the explicit matrix-product map U(theta) in U(2^m), m = |support| <= 3, built with numpy. (3) Choose a pin-set S of indices and target grid values g_i in (pi/4)Z (for i in S, g_i = the nearest multiple of pi/4 to the current theta_i, also trying 0 and +-pi/4 and +-pi/2 as alternatives), and solve min over the free angles theta_{not in S} of the phase-aligned residual d(theta) = min_phi || e^{i phi} U(theta_S = g_S, theta_free) - U(theta^0) ||_2 (operator 2-norm; phi eliminated analytically from the dominant eigenphase of U(theta)^dag U(theta^0)) with scipy.optimize.least_squares from 8 starts: theta^0 itself plus 7 random perturbations. (4) Greedy, largest-|theta| first: try to pin one more angle, keep the pin iff the refit residual d <= delta_w = 2e-6; on failure drop that index and continue with the next. Emit the window with the pinned angles written as exact Clifford/T gates (with_ops demotes pi/4 multiples) and the refitted free angles as rz. Cap the pass at 100 accepted windows so the total charge is <= 2e-4 of the 5e-4 approximation budget. One match = one window + its final pin-set, applied atomically.
cards.correctness: Nothing is claimed to be an identity: the rule is an approximation with an explicitly measured error, which is exactly what the 'approx' contract charges. The replacement window unitary U' = U(theta_S = g_S, theta_free*) satisfies, by construction of the accept test in step (4), min_phi ||e^{i phi} U' - U||_2 <= delta_w = 2e-6, and the frozen judge re-measures this same phase-aligned operator distance on the changed window and charges it; with <= 100 accepted windows the total charge is <= 2e-4 < eps/2 = 5e-4, and distances compose subadditively because the operator norm is submultiplicative and unitary-invariant: ||A_1...A_r - B_1...B_r|| <= sum_j ||A_j - B_j|| when all factors are unitary. Global phase is unobservable (invariant 6), hence the phi minimization is legitimate; the residual is computed on the true matrix, not on an angle-space proxy, so no first-order linearization enters the bound. The mechanism that makes the pins feasible at 2e-6 rather than at the O(pi/8) naive rounding error is parameter redundancy: the map theta -> U(theta) from a window with k angles into the (at most dim-of-local-orbit)-dimensional family it actually sweeps is generically non-injective whenever k exceeds that dimension (e.g. a window whose rotations, after Clifford conjugation, act about Paulis P, Q, PQ in one commuting frame sweeps a 2- or 3-parameter family however many rz ops are written), so the level set U(theta) = U(theta^0) is a positive-dimensional manifold and moving along it lets the free angles absorb a pinned angle's shift exactly up to numerics; only the *last* pins that leave the level set pay a real, measured approximation. Soundness does not depend on that redundancy existing: when it does not, the residual exceeds delta_w and the pin is simply dropped, so the rule degrades to a no-op rather than to an unsound rewrite. Cost side: pinning an angle to a multiple of pi/4 makes it exact under the metric's convention (pi/4 multiples are free), so N_Rz strictly drops and the runner's T-count gate decides the keep.
cards.trigger: Fires on any maximal contiguous window of the 1034-op list with support <= 3 qubits, <= 40 ops and >= 3 rz ops whose angle is not a multiple of pi/4, for which at least one greedy pin survives the residual test at 2e-6. On qpe_8 this is the dominant local pattern: the trigram census is saturated by short single- and two-wire sandwiches carrying several rotations each ('h rz rz' 42x, 'h rz h' 40x, 'rz h h' 40x, 'rz h rz' 28x, 'sdg h rz' 28x, 'h cx rz' 34x, 'cx rz h' 30x, 'cx t cx' 29x, 'cx tdg cx' 43x), and with 257 rz / 268 cx / 258 h over only 8 qubits the <=3-qubit support cut yields roughly 60-90 windows that together hold most of the 257 non-Clifford rotations. Windows are visited in descending rotation count so the fixed 2e-4 charge is spent where the most rotations can be retired per unit of error. No window is cut at an h or at a rotation, so the H density that limited the earlier phase-polynomial attempt (history attempt 1: 'segments end at every H, so few rotations pair up', measured 192 T against an estimate of 2700) does not gate this rule at all.
cards.expected_effect: Each surviving non-pi/4 rz costs gridsynth ~53 T at the current operating point (13603 T over 257 rotations), and every angle pinned to a multiple of pi/4 removes that rotation entirely: it becomes a literal z/s/sdg/t/tdg (or vanishes at 0) at zero T-cost beyond the Clifford layer. There is a second-order bonus: N_Rz appears in eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz, so retiring r rotations also relaxes the per-rotation tolerance for the survivors and shaves ~3 log2(257/(257-r)) T off each one (r = 50 gives ~0.9 T on each of ~207 survivors, ~190 T free). Mechanism check against the baselines: this is the first rule to spend any of the approximation budget on this circuit (the whole current book is exact), and BQSKit-DPF reaches 8020 against pyzx's exact-contract 11485 on the same input, i.e. about 3500 T on qpe_8 is reachable only by numerical window refitting rather than by rotation merging - which is precisely the mechanism here, reproduced with scipy least_squares instead of BQSKit instantiation. Estimate: 30-65 angles pinned across the window set (half the windows yielding at least one pin), i.e. ~1600-3450 T plus the eps_rz relief, so 13603 -> roughly 10300-12000. I deliberately quote the low-middle of that band as the point estimate: the one earlier attempt on this circuit overshot 14x because it assumed structural coincidences (shared parity labels) that the H density destroyed, whereas the quantity this rule depends on - per-window angle redundancy - is bounded below by nothing, so the honest expectation is that only windows with k >= 4 rotations on <= 2 qubits pin reliably. CNOT count and qubit count are unchanged (8 qubits), so the tie-breakers after T are neutral.
cards.source: E. Younis, K. Sen, K. Yelick, C. Iancu, 'QFAST / QSearch: Quantum circuit synthesis with numerical instantiation', IEEE QCE 2021, and E. Younis et al., 'BQSKit: Berkeley Quantum Synthesis Toolkit' - the instantiation-based re-fit of a fixed circuit template to a target unitary that underlies BQSKit's approximate passes; the angle-pinning / parameter-redundancy formulation follows L. Madden and A. Simonetto, 'Best approximate quantum compiling problems', ACM Trans. Quantum Computing 3(2), 2022, and the T-cost model of the pinned-vs-free angles is Ross-Selinger gridsynth (N. J. Ross, P. Selinger, 'Optimal ancilla-free Clifford+T approximation of z-rotations', QIC 16(11-12), 2016), in which multiples of pi/4 are exactly representable at zero cost.

cards.name: pauli_exponential_commutation_merge
cards.identity: Global Pauli-rotation normal form with commutation-reordering, then merge. (1) Sweep the op list left to right carrying a Clifford tableau C = product of all Clifford ops seen so far (h, s, sdg, x, z, cx, cz; t/tdg handled as rotations, see below). For every rotation op k at position p_k, acting as rz(theta_k) on wire q_k, compute its FRONT-FRAME Pauli P_k = C_k^dag Z_{q_k} C_k (C_k = the Clifford prefix before position p_k), with its sign eta_k in {+1,-1} taken from the tableau; so the op equals, as a factor commuted to the circuit's front, exp(-i eta_k theta_k P_k / 2) with P_k a signed n-qubit Pauli that may be X-, Y- or Z-type and may be multi-qubit. The whole circuit is then exactly U = [prod_{k=1..R} exp(-i eta_k theta_k P_k / 2)] . C_final, in op order, R = number of rotation ops, C_final = full Clifford product. (2) MATCH: a pair j < k of rotation records with P_j = +-P_k (as unsigned Pauli strings, sign folded into s = eta_j eta_k (+-1)) such that P_k COMMUTES with P_i for every intermediate rotation record j < i < k. (3) APPLY, in the ORIGINAL op list, with no Clifford touched and no resynthesis: delete op p_k, and set op p_j's angle to theta_eff = (theta_j + s . theta_k) reduced mod 2pi into (-pi, pi]; if theta_eff == 0 delete op p_j as well, if theta_eff is a multiple of pi/4 with_ops demotes it to z/s/sdg/t/tdg (a FULL removal of a synthesized rotation). (4) Rotation records include the explicit t/tdg ops (theta = +-pi/4), but a pair is only reported when at least one member is a non-pi/4-multiple rz, and a (rz, t/tdg) pair only when theta_eff lands on the pi/4 grid, so every reported match strictly lowers N_Rz. Matches are enumerated by descending |theta_j| + |theta_k| and are reported one at a time (positions recomputed after each accepted application).
cards.correctness: Two facts, both exact. (a) Frame transport: for any Clifford C and Pauli P, C exp(-i a P/2) = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2) C, an identity because C exp(X) C^dag = exp(C X C^dag) and Clifford conjugation maps Paulis to signed Paulis; iterating it over the prefix moves every rotation to the front of the circuit, leaving the Clifford product C_final at the end. cards.name: hamming_weight_phasing_same_angle_groups
cards.identity: Same-angle Pauli-rotation groups are replaced by one Hamming-weight phasing gadget. (1) Reuse the front-frame machinery of the accepted pauli_exponential_commutation_merge: sweep the op list carrying the Clifford tableau and give every rotation op k (rz/t/tdg at position p_k, wire q_k, angle theta_k) its front-frame signed Pauli P_k = C_k^dag Z_{q_k} C_k, eta_k in {+1,-1}, so the circuit is exactly [prod_k exp(-i eta_k theta_k P_k/2)] . C_final. (2) GROUP: a set G = {k_1<...<k_m}, m >= 5, of rotation records whose angles agree up to sign modulo 2pi (|theta| equal to 1e-9, eta folded in), whose Paulis P_{k_j} pairwise COMMUTE, and such that every P_{k_j} commutes with the Pauli of every rotation record strictly between k_1 and k_m (so the whole group can be slid, exactly, into one layer at position p_{k_1}). The m Paulis need not be equal - that is the point. (3) EMIT at p_{k_1}, deleting all m original rotation ops: (a) a Clifford D that simultaneously diagonalizes the commuting set, D P_{k_j} D^dag = Z^{v_j} (symplectic Gram-Schmidt over F2; h/s/sdg/cx only, zero T); (b) m clean ancillas a_1..a_m, each loaded with its parity by CNOTs from supp(v_j) into a_j, plus an X on a_j when eta_j theta_j has the opposite sign to the group's reference theta; (c) a Hamming-weight network that writes |a_1..a_m| into b = ceil(log2(m+1)) clean weight qubits w_0..w_{b-1} using m - popcount(m) Gidney temporary-AND full adders (and_compute, 4 T each); (d) exactly b rotations: phase gate P(2^i theta) i.e. rz(-2^i theta) on w_i, i = 0..b-1, each written as rz (with_ops demotes any that land on the pi/4 grid); (e) the adder network reversed with measurement-based and_uncompute (0 T) and the parity CNOTs/X undone, returning all ancillas to |0>; (f) D^dag. (b) Once gathered, prod_{j=1..m} exp(-i eta_j theta_j P_{k_j}/2) = exp(-i (theta/2) sum_j s_j P_{k_j}) with s_j = +-1, because the P_{k_j} pairwise commute and all |theta_j| = theta. cards.trigger: Any set of >= 5 rotation records with equal |angle| mod 2pi whose front-frame Paulis pairwise commute and each commute with every intervening rotation Pauli. cards.name: and_monomial_phase_polynomial_resynthesis
cards.identity: Re-express a diagonal phase block in the MONOMIAL (Reed-Muller) basis instead of the parity (Walsh) basis, and pay for each monomial with one rotation on an AND-ancilla rather than with 2^d - 1 parity rotations. (1) SEGMENT: cut the op list into maximal contiguous blocks that are Hadamard-free on the wires they touch, over {cx, x, z, s, sdg, t, tdg, rz} (equivalently: use the front-frame machinery of the accepted pauli_exponential_commutation_merge to gather a set of rotation records whose front-frame Paulis pairwise commute and commute with every intervening rotation Pauli, then apply the free Clifford D that simultaneously diagonalizes them; both entry points end with a diagonal block). (2) LABEL: sweep the block carrying, per wire q, the affine parity label (p[q] in F2^n over the block's INPUT basis variables x_1..x_n, plus sign bit c[q]): cx a,b does p[b] ^= p[a], c[b] ^= c[a]; x a flips c[a]. Each rotation op k on wire q with angle theta_k (t = pi/4, tdg = -pi/4, s, sdg, z included) contributes, up to an x-independent phase, the real phase term s_k theta_k * y_k(x) where y_k(x) = <p_k, x> mod 2 and s_k = (-1)^{c[q]}: the block's phase function is f(x) = sum_k s_k theta_k (<p_k,x> mod 2), and the block equals [diag e^{i f(x)}] . L where L is the block's own CX/X linear permutation (Clifford, untouched). (3) TRANSFORM: expand each XOR into the multilinear monomial basis, (xor_{i in S} x_i) = sum_{nonempty T subset S} (-2)^{|T|-1} prod_{i in T} x_i, and collect f(x) = sum_T c_T prod_{i in T} x_i with c_T = (-2)^{|T|-1} * sum over rotations k with T subset supp(p_k) of s_k theta_k, each c_T reduced mod 2pi into (-pi, pi]; drop c_T = 0. (4) COST TEST: let R = number of rotation ops in the block, M = number of surviving monomials T, A = number of 2-input AND gadgets needed to compute all monomials of degree >= 2 in a shared Gray/prefix order (a degree-d monomial needs d-1 ANDs; prefixes are shared, each AND 4 T with measurement-based uncompute at 0 T). Fire the rule only if M * C_rz + 4 * A < R * C_rz, with C_rz the metric's current gridsynth cost per non-grid rotation; monomials whose c_T is already a multiple of pi/4 count 0 on the left (with_ops demotes them). (5) EMIT, at the block's start (where every wire literally holds its input variable x_i), deleting all R rotation ops and leaving L bit-for-bit: for each monomial of degree 1, rz(c_T) on wire i; for each monomial of degree >= 2, compute prod_{i in T} x_i into a clean ancilla with the and_compute ladder (reusing shared prefix ancillas), apply rz(c_T) on the top ancilla, and uncompute the ladder with measurement-based and_uncompute (0 T, Clifford fix-ups classically controlled), returning every ancilla to |0>; then the original L, then (front-frame entry only) D^dag. Ancillas are allocated per block and reused across blocks, since each block returns them to |0>. One match = one block with its monomial list, applied atomically; blocks are enumerated by descending predicted saving.
cards.correctness: Four exact steps, no approximation claimed anywhere. (a) Diagonalization: rz/z/s/sdg/t/tdg are diagonal and cx/x are computational-basis permutations, so a Hadamard-free block acts as diag(e^{i f(x)}) . L; conjugating Z_q backwards through the CX/X prefix gives (-1)^{c[q]} Z^{p[q]} (CX^dag Z_t CX = Z_c Z_t, X^dag Z X = -Z), which is exactly the label recursion, and rz(theta) on a wire whose value is y gives phase e^{-i theta/2} e^{i theta y} - the factor e^{-i theta/2} is x-independent, hence a global phase (invariant 6). The front-frame entry point is the already-verified transport identity C exp(-i a P/2) = exp(-i a (C P C^dag)/2) C plus simultaneous diagonalization of a pairwise-commuting Pauli set by a zero-T Clifford D (symplectic Gram-Schmidt), both exact. (b) The basis change is an identity of real functions on {0,1}^n, not a numerical fit: for x_i in {0,1}, xor_{i in S} x_i = (1 - prod_{i in S}(1 - 2x_i))/2 = sum_{nonempty T subset S} (-2)^{|T|-1} prod_{i in T} x_i, verified term by term; summing over rotations gives c_T, and the multilinear representation of a function on {0,1}^n is unique, so the emitted phase function equals f on every one of the 2^n basis states. The only floating point is the summation of angles, the same level of arithmetic as the already-accepted merge rules; reduction of c_T mod 2pi is exact up to global phase. (c) Monomial on an ancilla: with the ancilla holding m = prod_{i in T} x_i, rz(c_T) on it applies e^{i c_T m} up to the x-independent e^{-i c_T/2}, which is precisely the monomial's contribution; the ancilla is a function of the data only, so the phase is correct in every branch. (d) Resource discipline: ANDs are Gidney temporary-AND gadgets whose measurement-based uncompute applies, on each measurement branch, either identity or a classically controlled Clifford fix-up, so every branch realizes the SAME operator with the SAME phase on the data and leaves every ancilla in |0> - exactly the relaxed contract the judge checks, and the identical pattern to the accepted and_ancilla_ccz_lowering_with_measured_uncompute. The linear permutation L and all Hadamards are left untouched, so nothing outside the block changes.
cards.trigger: Any Hadamard-free block (or commuting front-frame group) whose phase function has strictly fewer surviving monomials, charged with 4 T per AND, than it has rotation ops - computed, not guessed, by step (4). The minimal and most frequent instance is the controlled-phase signature: a single CPhase(phi) is written by TKET as THREE non-grid rotations of half-angle about the parities u, v and u^v (the 'rz ... cx rz cx ... rz' pattern), whose monomial form is the single term (phi) x_u x_v, so 3 synthesized rotations collapse to 1 rotation + 1 AND. This pattern is what qpe_8 is made of: the controlled-U^{2^k} ladder and the inverse-QFT ladder are nothing but controlled-phase gates, and the op census shows exactly their TKET expansion (268 cx, 257 rz, 'h cx rz' 34x, 'cx rz h' 30x, 'h rz rz' 42x, 'rz h rz' 28x, 'cx t cx' 29x, 'cx tdg cx' 43x), with the angle histogram's half/double families (0.331877 vs 7.097863, 1.999991 vs 10.566379, each x15) being the half-angle partners of one CPhase. Why this is not blocked by the limitations already measured on this circuit: attempt 1 failed because merging needs two rotations with the EQUAL parity label and H-bounded segments rarely contain such a pair (3 applications, 192 T); this rule needs no equality and no pair - the three parities of one CPhase are DIFFERENT, sit in one short H-free run separated only by cx, and still collapse. Degree-1 coefficients additionally aggregate the contributions of every parity containing that variable, so parity merging is subsumed as a special case, and some degree-1 coefficients land on the pi/4 grid and cost nothing.
cards.expected_effect: A surviving non-grid rz costs gridsynth ~45 T at the current operating point (11485 T over ~250 surviving rotations). Each collapsed degree-2 monomial retires 2 rotations and pays 4 T: ~86 T net. Each degree-3 monomial (a doubly-controlled phase, 7 parities in the Walsh basis) retires 6 rotations for 8 T: ~262 T net, and QPE's controlled-U blocks on a multi-qubit eigenstate register do contain such terms. CNOT count is roughly unchanged (the parity ladders are replaced by AND ladders); qubit count rises by the maximum AND depth, a handful of clean ancillas reused across blocks (8 -> ~10-12), which is the third tie-breaker, after T. Calibration against history: the two previous estimates on this circuit assumed structural coincidences (shared parity labels, per-window angle redundancy) that the input did not contain, and I am deliberately not doing that - the structure this rule needs (a phase term of degree >= 2) is visible in the op list itself and is checked arithmetically before any edit, so the downside is a no-op rather than a miss. Conservative count: if only the clean, locally contiguous CPhase triples collapse - 20 to 40 of them - the saving is 1700 to 3400 T, i.e. 11485 -> roughly 8100-9800, which is the band BQSKit-DPF reaches (8020) and which no exact-contract pass on this input has reached. I quote the low end as the point estimate.
